title: Arrange
description: Line the selection up, flip it, and restack it — exactly, without dragging.

bubble.title: Arrange: placement without dragging
bubble.body: Arrange lines shapes up, flips them, and stacks them in order. Everything in this section acts on the selection — no dragging, no eyeballing.

bubble.title: Watch: align and flip
bubble.body: Press Watch demo: the program draws two offset rectangles, selects both, aligns their left edges, and flips the pair.

demo.title: Two offset rectangles
demo.body: Drawing two rectangles that line up neither by edge nor by centre.

demo.title: Select all
demo.body: Selecting every shape, so Arrange has something to act on.

demo.title: Align left
demo.body: Aligning the left edges. The second rectangle slides to meet the first.

demo.title: Flip horizontal
demo.body: Flipping the pair sideways — they swap places around their shared centre.

demo.title: Done
demo.body: Aligned and flipped, without a single drag.

bubble.title: Select both shapes
bubble.body: The demo's two rectangles are on the canvas. Click one, then Shift+click the other, so both are selected.

bubble.title: Align their bottoms
bubble.body: With both selected, click Align Bottom in the Arrange section (or Object ▸ Align ▸ Align Bottom). The lower shape pulls the other down to its edge.

bubble.title: Flip them
bubble.body: Both are still selected. Click Flip Vertical in the Arrange section (or Object ▸ Flip ▸ Flip Vertical) — the pair swaps places around their shared centre.

bubble.title: Now just one
bubble.body: Click a single shape, without Shift, so only it is selected. Stacking order is a one-shape-at-a-time decision.

bubble.title: Send it to the back
bubble.body: Choose Object ▸ Order ▸ Send to Back. Where shapes overlap, the other one now shows in front.

bubble.title: Selection in, placement out
bubble.body: Arrange acts on the selection: align it, flip it, stack it. The status box always names what is selected, so you know what will move before you commit.
